body: Of the 43 group profiles reviewed, at least 10 had a public family or control dispute: Ambani (2002-05 split), Tata (Mistry ouster 2016, SC 2021; trustee split 2025-26), Birla-Lodha (Priyamvada will, 2004 onwards; Calcutta HC Dec-2023), Murugappa (2019-23, settled), Godrej (amicable split 2024), TVS (2020 partition; Venu Srinivasan family dispute open in Oct-2026), Kalyani (Hikal and Sulochana Kalyani will; SC mediator Jul-2026), Hinduja (2014 letter litigation; Gopichand died Nov-2025), Bajaj (old branch splits), and the Singh brothers vs. their spiritual-guru lenders. Pattern: disputes that stayed at the family holdco level and left listed companies' cash alone (Godrej, Murugappa, Tata) did little lasting harm to minorities. Where the dispute froze strategy or control (Birla-Lodha: ~20 years of litigation over Birla Corp and others) or touched listed boards (Tata-Mistry 2016; Kalyani-Hikal), it raised uncertainty and holdco discounts. Settlements take 3-20 years. A pre-announced split with listed companies untouched and a non-compete (Godrej 2024) is the good template. Signals: deaths of patriarchs without a public will, 'family arrangement' documents of disputed legal status (Hikal 1993-94; Hinduja 2014), trust structures with vague beneficiaries (TVS Holdings' VS Trust at 66.55%), and women heirs excluded from holdco boards (Murugappa). Investor read: price the dispute as a governance discount, not a business impairment, unless listed-company cash, board control or a forced stake sale is in play.
title: Family succession disputes: frequent, slow, and mostly a holdco-level risk if the listed companies are ring-fenced
